findings.detail: These lecture-01 questions are supported by lecture04 pages 3/4/8/11/12 and, for workload versus architecture, lecture07 pages 2–6. Those local extracted pages were read. They are previews, not material claimed to originate on lecture01 pages 3/4/8/11/12.

Physical lecture02 page13 (printed slide14) says aggregates can only occur in SELECT; physical page17 (printed slide18) explicitly places an aggregate in HAVING. Canonical question/explanation correctly reads the deck together; VI preserves that reconciliation.

Physical lecture03 page9 says set projection results in fewer rows. Canonical explanation correctly qualifies that projection may preserve cardinality when projected tuples remain distinct; VI preserves the qualification rather than treating the slide phrase as universal.

Text on lecture04 physical page9 explicitly says cross-cutting modules, and lecture05 pages20/21 explicitly say set pinned, set reference bit and advance clock. These text statements support the answers. Diagram geometry and visible bit placement were not freshly inspected; extraction alone is not a full visual diagram audit.

Question asks how to use hardware prices and latency figures but cites only physical page23, which is the broader conclusion and contains no price/latency table. Specific figures appear on pages12/17/20/21. Answer is sensible and matches current lesson caveat, but root should consider widening page references to 12/17/20/21/23 rather than presenting page23 as the sole specific evidence. Canonical citation left untouched.

limitations: No fresh diagram visual audit. Extracted text supports the rules; graphical arrows/ref-bit positions are not independently accepted.
No fresh external-paper verification. Cross-document quiz sources were reviewed in sibling private-source-review extracted physical-page files.
